text:
Beau Lamarre-Condon’s fate is in the hands of his peers as the 12-person jury in his double murder trial has been sent off to deliberate.
The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Jesse Baird and his new partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
But it will be up to 12 jurors, who have viewed every exhibit and listened to every witness – including the accused – to deliver a verdict.
They were sent off to deliberate on Wednesday morning, 10 weeks after the trial first began.
The jury was empanelled in September at Sydney’s King St court house, with three additional people picked to account for potential juror drop out due to reasons such as illness.
But the entire 15-person jury stood strong through two months of evidence, and shortly before deliberations began, three jurors were eliminated by ballot.
Justice Natalie Adams on Tuesday said the process could be “a little brutal”.
She acknowledged jurors on long trials often form friendships with each other, and can become emotional if they do not make it into the final jury.
The eliminated jurors are barred from contacting the jury until they come to a verdict.
But Adams maintained they had still played an important role in the trial.

גורלו של ביו למאר-קונדון נתון בידי חבר המושבעים, אשר פרש לדיונים לאחר משפט בן עשרה שבועות בגין רצח כפול. שוטר העבר נאשם כי ירה למוות בג'סי ביירד ובבן זוגו החדש לוק דייוויס באמצעות נשקו המשטרתי בפברואר 2024. למאר-קונדון כפר באשמה בשתי עבירות רצח ובעבירת פריצה מחמירה.

חבר המושבעים, המונה 12 חברים לאחר צמצומו משלושה עשר משתתפים, בחן את כלל הראיות והעדויות במשפט שנפתח בספטמבר. השופטת נטלי אדמס הודתה כי התהליך היה מורכב עבור המושבעים שנקשרו זה לזה, אך הדגישה את חשיבות תפקידם בהכרעת הדין.
